correctness.rationale: For every fixed positive j, the mixed moment m(m-1)Q-m²P_rP_s is derived from one- and two-box occupancy probabilities. The log-factor ratio has a uniform m^-2 expansion for N/m in compact positive intervals, with F=(alpha-a)^2/alpha and G(a)=1 at r=j²,s=(j+1)²,a=j(j+1). This yields the unscaled limiting covariance including the strict sign regions; the boundary signs are not asserted. A standalone standard-library verifier checked 720 exhaustive finite exact covariance identities, 300 critical polynomial identities, and 14 numerical diagnostics. Finite checks are supplemental and do not replace the Taylor proof.

originality.rationale: The classical exact occupancy moments and fixed-load first covariance coefficient are explicitly excluded from the novel claim. A double cancellation for precisely consecutive square indices requires retaining the next asymptotic order and tuning load within m^-1/2; the resulting universal order-one parabolic covariance window was not identified in the primary source sections inspected, nor in the recoverable closest indexed records. The historical multivariate literature may contain implicit higher-order expansions, so this is a qualified best-knowledge priority assessment.

value.rationale: The distinct square-index frequency pairs are exactly all positive-integer tangencies of the classical fixed-density covariance coefficient. Their leading order disappears, but the next coefficient is universally +1 in the normalized log ratio, producing a positive order-one mixed covariance and an explicit reentrant parabolic window of width m^-1/2. This natural dependence boundary matters when interpreting frequency-of-frequencies data; it is not an arbitrary fixed-size computation or merely an arithmetic reparameterization.
